text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- A lively debate broke out in Parliament before regular business yesterday over who deserves credit for Hungary's progress towards Euro-Atlantic integration.
- The leadership of the Hungarian Calvinist Church yesterday criticized the bill on church financing.
- Government officials placed a joint wreath at the Budapest statue of Imre Nagy, prime minister during the 1956 uprising, marking the 39th anniversary of his execution.
- The majority of Christian Democratic MPs support Zsolt Semjen for party president, although no official stance was taken on the matter yesterday.

- Defense Minister Gyorgy Keleti held talks in Warsaw Monday on the NATO accession process, possible joint military purchases and bilateral technological cooperation with his Polish counterpart Stanislaw Dobrzanski.
- The Nordic Investment Bank will extend credits to Hungary's public and private development initiatives.
- The British company PowerGen will establish a $250 million power plant beside one it already owns in the southern outskirts of Budapest.

- The German consortiums RWE Energie and EVS plan to invest more than Ft 40 billion in the Matrai power plant over the next few years and nearly Ft 280 billion in establishing a new, lignite-fired facility, also in northern Hungary.
- OTP, K&H Bank and Mezobank privatisation on the horizon.
- OTP Bank Rt. has dismissed three top officials of its regional headquarters in Nograd County, northern Hungary.
